Energetics, Incorporated (2000). Energy and Environmental Profile of the U.S. Iron and Steel Industry. Prepared by Nancy Margolis and Ross Brindle for the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Industrial Technologies, Report DOE/EE-0229, August 2000.

Region: United States, base year 1998 (MECS 1994 for Table 1-5). Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 8). The report holds no capex, opex, capacity or technology cost data; it is a statistical profile. Loaded: energy and CO2 per t of product for coke ovens, sinter strand, blast furnace, BOF, EAF, continuous and ingot casting, reheat furnace, hot rolling, pickling, cold rolling, annealing, ladle metallurgy and hot-dip galvanneal. All are US-average figures built from industry totals divided by 1998 production (derived per t by the extractor from printed totals, with the printed per-ton value quoted in each note). MMBtu/short ton converted to GJ/tonne with x1.055056/0.907185; lb CO2 per short ton to t/t with /2000. TRAPS: (1) Electricity in the printed per-ton columns is converted at 10,500 Btu/kWh (primary equivalent); kWh were taken from the printed kWh totals and footnotes (sinter, BF, coke and BOF kWh partly assumptions in the report, e.g. 35, 20 and 21 kWh/ton) or back-calculated from MMBtu. (2) Table 1-13 and Chapter 3-6 CO2 intensities are per ton of STEEL, not per ton of process product; per-product values derived from printed totals. (3) Table 4-1 coke oven gas printed 0.1 MMBtu/ton conflicts with its own total (0.007); derived value used. (4) Table 7-1 cold rolling 0.7 is printed under the Fuel row. (5) Natural gas is split between BOF and EAF by assumption (Table 4-1 note c). (6) Table 1-4 typos (fuel oil units, BF gas recovered 1,997 vs 1,197 x 10^9 ft3). (7) Heating-value basis not stated; gases converted at fixed Btu/ft3. (8) No BOF gas credit given. Not loaded: criteria pollutants, effluents, wastes, TRI data, emission factors for non-GHG species.
